LLM Adaptation: Papers looking to modify or manipulate an LLM for single-generation hardware design.
LLM Pipeline: Processes that orchestrate prompts, tools, or post-processing around a single LLM run to improve design outcomes.
Benchmark: Papers releasing resources or studies intended to measure or standardize LLM performance in EDA tasks.
RTL Generation: Synthesizing functional HDL code (e.g., Verilog, VHDL) from natural language specifications at module or hierarchical level.
Code Repair: Identifying and automatically fixing syntax errors or functional bugs in existing HDL code.
Simulation & Verification: Generating verification artifacts, including testbenches, assertions (SVA), or test vectors to validate hardware designs.
EDA Script Generation: Automating EDA workflows by having LLMs write or modify tool directives, scripts, or configuration files.
Dataset Construction: Producing organized collections of ground-truth hardware designs and inputs for systematic testing or improvement of LLM systems.
Bug Analysis: Automating the analysis of bug reports or verification logs to provide human-readable summaries of design errors.
Performance Prediction: Using LLMs to estimate PPA (Power, Performance, Area) metrics or other design characteristics early in the flow without running full synthesis.
Design Space Exploration: Using LLMs to explore or select design configurations to improve objectives (such as PPA or design flow parameters).
Tree Search: Algorithms that generate multiple candidate solutions and traverse them using search strategies (e.g., Monte Carlo Tree Search, Beam Search) to find the optimal code or design.
LLM Multi-Agency: Frameworks involving the interaction of multiple distinct LLM instances (agents), often assigning them specific roles (e.g., designer, verifier) to collaborate on a task.
Planning & Decomposition: Approaches that let the model plan and decompose complex designs into organized steps or hierarchical components.
Retrieval Augmented Generation: Systems that query an external knowledge base to provide relevant context to the LLM during generation.
Supervised Fine-Tuning: Training a pre-trained model on a labeled dataset of domain-specific examples.
Reinforcement Learning: Optimization methods using reward signals (e.g. from simulation/synthesis/implementation results or compiler feedback) to guide the model's policy updates.
Summarisation: Methods that condense HDL, logs, or documentation into concise natural-language descriptions for downstream use.
Eval. Suite: Methodologies and benchmarks proposed for scoring or assessing model performance.
In-Context Learning: Methods relying on prompt engineering (e.g. few-shot examples) included in the context window to guide model behavior without weight updates.
Iterative Feedback Loop: Techniques where the model/framework critiques and iteratively refines its own output based on internal feedback, prompt iteration, or EDA design flow results.
Continued Pre-training: Extending the training of a base foundation model on a large corpus of hardware-specific languages (Verilog, VHDL, SystemVerilog) to improve domain understanding.
Techniques used to artificially expand or diversify the training/prompting dataset (e.g. LLM data generation, HDL masking) to improve model robustness.
Generator: LLM produces a design once in forward pass; human decides what happens next
Agent: LLM iterates with EDA tool feedback within a fixed pipeline
Orchestrator: LLM dynamically decides which tools and stages to envoke.
